title: Lock both zip pullers of a hard-shell suitcase into its built-in lock
instruction: Close the suitcase's zip up to its lock and lock both zip pullers into the lock, then let go.
context: This task does not test zipping cloth: the case is a hard shell and is already shut, so its two rigid shells hold the zip straight. It tests the last step: locking the zip into the case's built-in TSA lock. Each puller hangs loose on a hinge. The robot must draw each slider to its end stop, swing the puller flat along the zip, and push it square into a sprung slot until the catch holds. A puller pushed in crooked swings away on its hinge, and one pushed only part way is not held. Real case: the Samsonite Freeform Spinner Carry-On (54.6 x 36.8 x 22.9 cm, 2.59 kg, integrated TSA lock; samsonite.ca). Its lock instructions say "Place the zippers into the Zipper Housing". TSA screened 904 million people at US airport checkpoints in 2024 (tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes/2024). Extending a suitcase's telescoping handle, or pressing a case's lever latches shut, is a different skill: here a small loose part is lined up with a 4 mm slot and seated against a spring.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of the table and a fixed camera above it. Positions in cm: x forward from the arm bases, y to the left, heights above the table top. Suitcase: a closed hard-shell carry-on spinner sized after the Samsonite Freeform Spinner Carry-On, 55 x 35 x 23 cm, 2.8 kg, blue polypropylene shell, lying on its back (as after packing), free on the table. A black carry handle, 18 x 6 x 2.5 cm, on its top face (drawn only: it cannot be touched). Reference pose: its long side toward the robot, near side at x 30, centred on y 0 (it covers x 30 to 65, y -27.5 to 27.5). The zip runs round the case between its two shells at 11.5 cm height; along the near side it is straight. The case is closed, so the two shells hold the zip's two tooth rows in line. Built-in TSA zip lock (as on that case) in the middle of the near side, on the zip line: black ABS housing 70 mm along the zip, 44 mm tall, standing 18 mm out, three red dials left at the factory code. Each end of the housing has a slot for one puller, 14 mm tall, 4 mm wide, 26 mm deep along the zip, its centre 10 mm out from the shell, its first 4 mm widened by 1.5 mm each way. In each slot a spring catch: a 4 x 4 mm plunger 13.5 mm in from the slot's mouth that crosses the slot from its outer wall, 3.5 mm into it, pressed in by a spring (2.0 N at rest, 3.4 N when lifted fully), flat on the side toward the slot's bottom and with a 30 degree ramp toward the mouth. Two zip sliders, zinc, 30 x 16 mm and 8 mm high off the shell, 12 g, one each side of the lock (A on the robot's left, B on its right), each running along the zip to its end stop where its front meets the housing's end; drawing a slider takes 3 N. Each slider carries a puller: a zinc tab 12 mm wide and 2.5 mm thick, 35 mm from its hinge pin (at the slider's middle) to its tip and 4 mm behind the pin, 6 g, with a 5 x 5 mm hole 26 to 31 mm from the pin. The pin is square to the case's side, so the tab swings from lying flat along the zip one way, through pointing straight out, to lying flat the other way. Fully in, a tab's tip is 20 mm inside its slot and the catch sits in its hole. Start, drawn from the trial's seed: the case moved up to 3 cm in x and in y and turned up to 12 degrees either way about the vertical; each slider 3 to 7 cm short of its end stop; each tab at 15 to 75 degrees from pointing straight out, toward the lock (as left by the last pull), each drawn on its own. Reference start: sliders 5 cm short, tabs at 45 degrees. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers. The screenshot shows seed 0's start.
scoring: Per side (A and B), up to 0.5: 0.15 if the slider is within 2 mm of its end stop; +0.15 if the puller lies within 10 degrees of flat along the zip toward the lock with its tip at least 10 mm into its slot; +0.20 if its tip is also at least 18 mm in and the catch is down in its hole (in a real trial: a 5 N pull on a luggage scale along the zip away from the lock does not draw it out; in simulation: the plunger is lifted less than 1 mm). Score = A + B. The trial scores 0 if the case was pushed more than 10 cm or tipped more than 10 degrees, or if either gripper ends within 30 mm of a slider, puller or catch. Read at the end of the run; the run ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s. Outcomes per side: nothing done 0; slider at the stop with its puller swung out or jammed crooked 0.15; puller part way in, short of the catch, slider not at the stop 0.15; puller in but the catch not down, slider at the stop 0.30; caught 0.50. Real trial tools: a ruler, a pen mark on each puller 10 mm and 18 mm from its tip, a luggage scale.
reset_notes: Reset: press the lock's release to free both pullers, draw each slider back to its drawn gap (3 to 7 cm short of the housing, measured with a ruler), set each tab to its drawn angle toward the lock, and put the case at its drawn pose. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at real size and mass. The catch works by contact: a sprung plunger rides up the puller's tip and drops into its hole; nothing attaches by a rule. Simplified: zip teeth and cloth are not simulated (the case is closed); each slider runs on a straight joint with 3 N friction. One hinge per puller. Case within 2 cm and 0.2 kg of the real one. Slot and catch sizes are typical, not measured; dials not modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run, seed 0: 0.0 (1,200 steps). Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (841 to 996 steps). Wrong outcomes: fixed plan 0.0; pullers pushed in crooked 0.3; pushed in part way 0.0.
